q.t: What is an interval?
q.e: An interval measures how far apart two notes are.

q.t: On the guitar, the easiest way to measure an interval is to…
q.e: One fret = one half step, so count frets from the lower note to the higher one.

q.t: How many half steps are in an octave?
q.e: An octave = all 12 notes.

q.t: How many half steps are in a perfect 5th?
q.e: Perfect 5th = 7 half steps (C → G).

q.t: How many half steps are in a major 3rd?
q.e: Major 3rd = 4 half steps (C → E).

q.t: How many half steps are in a minor 3rd?
q.e: Minor 3rd = 3 half steps (C → E♭).

q.t: C → D is a…
q.e: C(1) D(2) = a 2nd. C → C♯ → D = 2 half steps = major 2nd.

q.t: C → G is a…
q.e: C D E F G = 5 letters → a 5th. 7 half steps = perfect 5th.

q.t: Which interval sounds like the same note, higher?
q.e: The octave doubles the shakes per second — same note name.

q.t: Which interval is in the first jump of Twinkle Twinkle (twin-kle → twin-kle)?
q.e: In C: C C → G G. C to G is a perfect 5th.

q.t: How many half steps are in a perfect 4th?
q.e: Perfect 4th = 5 half steps (C → F).

q.t: C → F is a…
q.e: C D E F = 4 letters → a 4th. 5 half steps = perfect 4th.

q.t: C → E♭ is a…
q.e: 3 letters (C D E), but only 3 half steps → minor 3rd.

q.t: C → C♯ is a…
q.e: 1 half step = minor 2nd.

q.t: When naming an interval by letters, the first note counts as…
q.e: C → D: C is 1, D is 2 → a 2nd.

q.t: A major 3rd and a minor 3rd both span 3 letters. What is different?
o: The major one is one half step bigger
The minor one is one half step bigger
The major one has more letters
q.e: Major 3rd = 4 half steps; minor 3rd = 3. 'Minor' means smaller.

q.t: Which interval sounds the most clashing?
q.e: Two notes only a half step apart bump into each other — a buzzy clash.

q.t: How many half steps are in a tritone?
q.e: Tritone = 6 half steps — exactly half an octave.

q.t: In sargam, Sa → Pa is a…
q.e: Sa = 1, Pa = 5 → a perfect 5th, like C → G.

q.t: In sargam, Sa → Ma is a…
q.e: Sa = 1, Ma = 4 → a perfect 4th, like C → F.

q.t: A → C is a…
q.e: A B C = 3 letters. A → A♯ → B → C = 3 half steps → minor 3rd.

q.t: E → G♯ is a…
q.e: E F G = 3 letters. E → F → F♯ → G → G♯ = 4 half steps → major 3rd.

q.t: D → A is a…
q.e: D E F G A = 5 letters, 7 half steps → perfect 5th.

q.t: G → C is a…
q.e: G A B C = 4 letters, 5 half steps → perfect 4th.

q.t: C → A is a…
q.e: C D E F G A = 6 letters, 9 half steps → major 6th.

q.t: On the E, A and D strings, a perfect 5th above a note is…
q.e: Next string = 5 half steps; + 2 frets = 7 = perfect 5th.

q.t: On the E, A and D strings, a perfect 4th above a note is…
q.e: Neighbouring strings are tuned a perfect 4th (5 half steps) apart.

q.t: Low E string fret 3 is G. Where is the G one octave higher?
q.e: Octave shape: two strings up, 2 frets higher → D string fret 5.

q.t: Why do a perfect 5th's notes blend so smoothly?
o: They are on the same string
q.e: Small-number ratios line up often, so the notes don't clash.

q.t: Why does a minor 2nd sound clashing?
o: It is too high to hear
q.e: Big-number ratios line up rarely; in between, the waves keep bumping — a clash.

q.t: B → F is a…
q.e: B → C(1) → C♯(2) → D(3) → D♯(4) → E(5) → F(6). 6 half steps = tritone, not a perfect 5th.

q.t: F → E is a…
q.e: F to E = 7 letters, 11 half steps → major 7th.

q.t: A → G is a…
q.e: A to G = 7 letters, 10 half steps → minor 7th.

q.t: E → C is a…
q.e: E F G A B C = 6 letters. 8 half steps → minor 6th.

q.t: What note is a major 3rd above D?
q.e: D + 4 half steps: D♯, E, F, F♯.

q.t: What note is a perfect 5th above B?
G string fret 2 is A. Where is the perfect 5th (E) on the B string?
q.e: G → B is only 4 half steps, so add 3 frets (not 2): 4 + 3 = 7. B string fret 5 = E.

q.t: D string fret 2 is E. Where is the octave on the B string?
q.e: D → B is 5 + 4 = 9 half steps; add 3 frets for 12. Fret 5 of the B string = E.

q.t: Why are the 3rds called 'major' and 'minor' and not 'perfect'?
o: They come in two sizes, one half step apart
They are only used in sad songs
q.e: 3rds (and 2nds, 6ths, 7ths) have a bigger (major) and smaller (minor) form.

q.t: Why does the octave shape change when it crosses onto the B string?
o: G → B is 4 half steps, not 5
The B string is tuned to C
q.e: Losing one half step between strings means you add one extra fret to make up for it.
